title: [Python] BUG: Reading ORC segfaults on windows (if TZDIR isn't set)
body: I enabled ORC for PyArrow in a conda-forge Windows build. The test suite aborts as soon as it reaches test_dataset.py::test_orc_format while reading the dataset. The same segfault still appears with ORC 1.9.

symptoms_visible: On Windows, my PyArrow test suite terminates with a fatal Python abort when test_dataset.py::test_orc_format calls to_table.
The same abort occurs with ORC 1.9.
N0.label: N0 Windows ORC abort reported

symptoms_visible: The ORC read abort occurs in the same place with ORC 1.8.3 and 1.9, and it remains present with later Arrow and ORC combinations.
Windows wheel jobs also abort in test_dataset.py when the PyArrow ORC tests are actually enabled.
N1.label: N1 version-independent Windows reproduction established

symptoms_visible: In a local Windows build, every PyArrow ORC test aborts when it tries to read data.
With TZDIR set to the conda environment's share\zoneinfo directory, all of those ORC tests pass.
N2.label: N2 environment-sensitive reproduction measured

symptoms_visible: My Windows PyArrow build passes the test suite with ORC enabled when TZDIR points to %CONDA_PREFIX%\share\zoneinfo.
Without arranging that environment setting, ORC reads can still terminate the process.
N3.label: N3 workaround confirmed in reporter CI

symptoms_visible: The project's own Windows tests can pass after arranging timezone data there, but my conda package would still require TZDIR to be injected into each user environment to prevent the ORC read abort.
N3_x.label: N3_x project-test-only workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: The conda environment already has timezone data under its share\zoneinfo directory, but ORC does not use it automatically on Windows.
The package still needs an explicit TZDIR setting until the installed ORC library can locate that data itself.
N4.label: N4 production-safe upstream fix scoped

symptoms_visible: The upstream ORC change for locating the existing timezone database has been merged, so I expect to be able to package the fix without injecting TZDIR into every user environment; I have not yet reported a conda package retest without TZDIR.
N_terminal.label: terminal upstream change merged, downstream verification pending

question_patterns: Which ORC and Arrow versions have shown the same failure?
Does changing the ORC release alter where the test aborts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It happened in exactly the same place with ORC 1.8.3 and 1.9. I later still saw it with Arrow 13 and 14, and with Arrow 15.0.1 plus ORC 2.0.0.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failure occurs only with ORC 1.9; returning to 1.8.3 makes every test pass.
I reproduced the same abort with a different Arrow patch release, but at the same ORC read call.

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced in an Apache Windows job with the PyArrow ORC tests enabled?
Do the Windows wheel jobs fail at the same test once ORC coverage is actually turned on?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Once the missing PyArrow ORC test configuration was added, the Windows wheel jobs for Python 3.8 through 3.11 all aborted in test_dataset.py::test_orc_format.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c3, c7, c15-c17 establish persistence across releases. Maintainer reproduction from c14 is folded into the simulated affected-user side as permitted multi-user evidence; it describes the same Windows PyArrow ORC failure, not the unrelated build-dependency detour.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this in a local Windows build and narrow down which operation triggers it?
Please run the ORC tests locally and report the last operation reached before the process aborts.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it on my Windows PC. All of the PyArrow ORC tests fail when they try to read data, reaching the ORC adapter read path before the abort.

question_patterns: Can you vary the runtime environment around that read and report any setting that changes the result?
After inspecting the failing read path, is there an environment-only change that makes the same tests pass?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After `set TZDIR=%CONDA_PREFIX%\share\zoneinfo`, all of the ORC tests are green.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same tests still abort after setting TZDIR to an existing zoneinfo directory.
The tests pass when TZDIR points to a different valid copy of the same timezone database.
The build directory is on drive E instead of drive C.

edges.comment: Participant2's affected local Windows reproduction in c30 is folded into the user side. The answer preserves the raw observations: the read location and green tests after an environment change. The conclusion that ORC cannot locate its timezone database is reserved for the final solution's engineer inference.

question_patterns: Please apply the proposed environment setting in your affected CI build and report whether the full suite still aborts.
Can you rerun the original conda-forge Windows build with that runtime setting and tell me what happens?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can confirm that setting `TZDIR=%CONDA_PREFIX%\share\zoneinfo` makes PyArrow built with `PYARROW_WITH_ORC=1` pass the Windows test suite.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My original conda-forge job still aborts in test_orc_format with that setting.
The suite passes with the same setting supplied by the CI job configuration instead of the command prompt.

edges.comment: Reporter confirmation from c32-c33. This is a handler-requested configuration probe, so it remains a clarification-only measurement even though the environment setting is also a temporary workaround.

solution.intent: Handle timezone data only in Apache's Windows wheel and test jobs so those project-controlled jobs pass.
solution.concrete_example: Arrange timezone data or set the environment in the Windows wheel test job so the project's ORC-enabled test suite passes.
solution.inference_hint: A maintainer recognized that making Apache's own tests pass does not change lookup behavior in independently packaged user environments. That scope assessment is engineer-side reasoning, not a new reporter measurement.

edges.comment: Thread c47-c48: a pull request was initially treated as resolving the issue, but maintainers immediately clarified that it only hid the failure in project-controlled tests and left users exposed to the abort. This is the real falsified test-only resolution, not a release-logistics branch.

question_patterns: What timezone-data resources are already present in the affected package environment?
Would downstream packaging need to bundle new data, or is a usable database already installed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Conda-forge already provides the timezone database through its tzdata package under the environment prefix, so it should not need to be vendored again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no timezone database anywhere in the target environment, and conda cannot add one as a dependency.

question_patterns: What production behavior would avoid requiring every user to configure their environment manually?
Where should the runtime look for resources that are already installed with the environment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It should search a few reasonable candidate locations automatically, including the environment prefix's `share/zoneinfo` directory on Windows, rather than requiring TZDIR in every user environment.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Requiring every user to set the environment variable is acceptable for this package, so no automatic lookup is needed.
The same installed database is reachable through an equivalent path relative to site-packages.

question_patterns: Can this be implemented reliably in the Arrow layer, or does a dependency need to change?
After trying the downstream implementation, where does the remaining change need to live?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried to implement it in Arrow, but the recent guard around the old-ORC timezone-database check means the candidate search cannot really be done there. I opened an ORC-side change instead.

edges.comment: Reporter requirements and implementation attempt from c33, c39 and c54. The final fact that an upstream ORC change was proposed is placed in N4.volunteered_info because the reporter added it while explaining why the Arrow-side approach was blocked.

solution.intent: Fix the lookup in Apache ORC so Windows deployments can automatically find an existing local timezone database, including the conda environment's share/zoneinfo location, without requiring every user to set TZDIR; then verify the affected package against the merged change.
solution.concrete_example: Use the merged ORC-side path-search change so a conda Windows environment can locate its installed tzdata under the environment prefix. Rebuild the affected PyArrow package with that ORC change and rerun the ORC tests without TZDIR before declaring the user-facing issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The controlled contrast—ORC reads abort without the setting and all pass when TZDIR points at a valid conda zoneinfo directory—supports the diagnosis that ORC's timezone-database lookup is the trigger. Participant2 later explained that ORC defaults to a Unix path and consults TZDIR when that path fails; converting those observations into the root-cause diagnosis is engineer inference.

edges.comment: Final technical direction from c54-c55: the reporter's ORC-side candidate-path change was merged. The thread ends before the affected conda package is rebuilt and tested without TZDIR, so the terminal state records an upstream landing with downstream verification still pending rather than inventing a confirmed user resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: on Windows, Apache ORC cannot locate a usable timezone database through its existing lookup, and an ORC read can abort when that database is unavailable; the passing TZDIR-controlled runs ground this diagnosis.

Must recommend an ORC-side automatic search for an already installed timezone database, including the conda environment's share/zoneinfo location, instead of requiring TZDIR to be injected into every user environment.
Must not treat merely enabling ORC tests or arranging timezone data in Apache's own Windows CI and wheel jobs as the user-facing fix; that test-only approach leaves downstream users exposed.
Must not claim that changing ORC or Arrow versions alone fixes the issue, since the same abort was observed across the tested 1.8.3, 1.9 and 2.0.0-era combinations.

Must ask for the affected conda Windows package to be rebuilt and retested without TZDIR using an ORC build containing the path-search change before declaring the issue fully resolved; the thread only confirms that the upstream change merged.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical packaging maintainer familiar with conda-forge, CMake build flags, Windows CI, PyArrow feature configuration, dependency layouts, and upstreaming fixes.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, evidence-driven, and collaborative; reports exact version combinations and CI outcomes, challenges test-only fixes that do not protect users, and proposes packaging-compatible upstream behavior.
